chunks: And through it, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Ali ibn al-Harith ibn al-Mughira, from his father, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah: 'Will there be a period during which the Muslims do not know their Imam?' He said: 'It is said so.' I said: 'What will we do then?' He said: 'If that occurs, then hold fast to the previous one until the next one becomes clear to you.'

key_terms.إِمَام: Imam, the divinely appointed leader and guide
key_terms.الْأَمْر الْأَوَّل: The previous matter/Imam, referring to the Imam who preceded the period of absence
key_terms.فَتْرَة: A period of gap or intermission, specifically referring to the time between Imams or before the appearance of the Mahdi

ai.seo_question: What should Muslims do during the period when they do not know who their Imam is?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (as) addresses the concept of a gap in leadership (fitrat al-imamah) where the Muslims may not immediately recognize their Imam. The Imam instructs them to maintain adherence to the preceding Imam's teachings and authority until the new Imam is clearly identified, a principle crucial for understanding the Great Occultation. This guidance ensures continuity of religious authority during periods of uncertainty and widespread absence.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (2) Abdullah bin Jibilla narrated from Ali bin al-Harith bin al-Mugheera that his father had said:

I asked Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as): “Will there be a time, in which the Muslims will not know who their imam is?” He said: “It is said so.” I said: “what will we do then?” He said: “If that occurs, then keep to the previous one until the next one becomes clear to you.”
